name: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Canadian bunchberry
records.summary: Cornus canadensis is a species of flowering plant in the dogwood family Cornaceae, native to eastern Asia and North America. Common names include Canadian dwarf cornel, Canadian bunchberry, quatre-temps, crackerberry, and creeping dogwood.
records.photo_credit: (c) rangerkelly, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by rangerkelly
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Spreading dogbane
records.summary: Apocynum androsaemifolium, the fly-trap dogbane or spreading dogbane, is a flowering plant in the Gentianales order.
records.photo_credit: (c) Thayne Tuason, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Box elder
records.summary: Acer negundo is a species of maple native to North America. In Canada it is commonly known as Manitoba maple and occasionally as elf maple.
records.photo_credit: (c) Евгений Егорейченков, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Евгений Егорейченков
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Common jewelweed
records.summary: Impatiens capensis, the orange jewelweed, common jewelweed, spotted jewelweed, spotted touch-me-not, or orange balsam, is an annual plant native to North America. It is common in bottomland soils, ditches, and along creeks, often growing side-by-side with its less common relative, Yellow Jewelweed (I. pallida).
records.photo_credit: (c) Melina Keighron, all rights reserved, uploaded by Melina Keighron
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Oval-leaved milkweed
records.summary: Asclepias ovalifolia, commonly called oval-leaved milkweed or dwarf milkweed, is a species of flowering plant in the milkweed genus and dogbane family (Apocynaceae). It is native to South Central Canada and the Northern Midwest of the United States.
records.photo_credit: (c) Janet Nelson, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-ND), uploaded by Janet Nelson
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Butterfly milkweed
records.summary: Asclepias tuberosa is a species of milkweed native to eastern North America. It is a perennial plant growing to 0.3–1 metre (1 ft 0 in–3 ft 3 in) tall, with clustered orange or yellow flowers from early summer to early autumn.
records.photo_credit: (c) Michael J. Papay, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Michael J. Papay
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Common Snowberry
records.summary: Symphoricarpos albus is a species of flowering plant in the honeysuckle family known by the common name common snowberry. It is native to North America, where it occurs across much of Canada and the northern and western United States.
records.photo_credit: (c) Steve Kelley, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Steve Kelley
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Prickly cucumber
records.summary: Echinocystis is a monotypic genus in the gourd family, Cucurbitaceae. The sole species is E. lobata, commonly called wild cucumber, prickly cucumber, or balsam apple.
records.photo_credit: (c) Monteregina (Nicole), some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-SA)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: American plum
records.summary: Prunus americana, commonly called the American plum, wild plum, or Marshall's large yellow sweet plum, is a species of Prunus native to North America from Saskatchewan and Idaho south to New Mexico and east to Québec, Maine and Florida.
records.photo_credit: (c) Ryan Byrne, all rights reserved, uploaded by Ryan Byrne
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Broadleaf cattail
records.summary: Typha latifolia (broadleaf cattail, bulrush, common bulrush, common cattail, cat-o'-nine-tails, great reedmace, cooper's reed, cumbungi) is a perennial herbaceous plant in the genus Typha. It is found as a native plant species in North and South America, Europe, Eurasia, and Africa.
records.photo_credit: (c) cgbb2004, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by cgbb2004
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Lodgepole pine
records.summary: Pinus contorta, with the common names lodgepole pine and shore pine, and also known as twisted pine, and contorta pine, is a common tree in western North America. It is common near the ocean shore and in dry montane forests to the subalpine, but is rare in lowland rain forests.
records.photo_credit: (c) Alison Northup, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Alison Northup
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Spotted coralroot
records.summary: Corallorhiza maculata, or spotted coralroot, is a North American coralroot orchid flower. Varieties are also known as western coralroot and summer coralroot.
records.photo_credit: (c) Julia Carr, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Julia Carr
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Common starlily
records.summary: Leucocrinum montanum, commonly known as the sand lily, common starlily or mountain lily, is the only species in the monotypic genus Leucocrinum, placed in the family Asparagaceae, and subfamily Agavoideae. It is native to the western United States, primarily in the Rocky Mountains and the Great Basin.
records.photo_credit: (c) Brent Miller, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-ND)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Red columbine
records.summary: Aquilegia canadensis (Canadian or Canada columbine, eastern red columbine, wild columbine) is an herbaceous perennial native to woodland and rocky slopes in eastern North America, prized for its red and yellow flowers. It readily hybridizes with other species in the genus Aquilegia.
records.photo_credit: (c) Sadie Hickey, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Sadie Hickey
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Red baneberry
records.summary: Actaea rubra (red baneberry, chinaberry, doll's eye) is a poisonous herbaceous flowering plant in the family Ranunculaceae, native to North America.
records.photo_credit: (c) Sherrie Snyder, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Sherrie Snyder
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Paper birch
records.summary: Betula papyrifera (paper birch, also known as white birch and canoe birch) is a short lived species of birch native to northern North America. Paper birch is named due to the thin white bark which often peels in paper like layers from the trunk.
records.photo_credit: (c) Joan Davis, all rights reserved, uploaded by Joan Davis
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Virginia creeper
records.summary: Parthenocissus quinquefolia, known as Virginia creeper, Victoria creeper, five-leaved ivy, or five-finger, is a species of flowering plant in the grape family, Vitaceae. It is native to eastern and central North America, from southeastern Canada and the eastern United States west to Manitoba and Utah, and south to eastern Mexico and Guatemala.
records.photo_credit: (c) Suzanne Cadwell, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Woodland strawberry
records.summary: Fragaria vesca, commonly called wild strawberry, woodland strawberry, Alpine strawberry, Carpathian Strawberry, European strawberry, or fraisier des bois, is a perennial herbaceous plant in the rose family that grows naturally throughout much of the Northern Hemisphere, and that produces edible fruits.
records.photo_credit: (c) Алексей Афонин, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Алексей Афонин
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Yellow lady's slipper
records.summary: Cypripedium parviflorum, commonly known as yellow lady's slipper, moccasin flower, or hairy yellow ladyslipper is a lady's slipper orchid found in North America.
records.photo_credit: (c) arethusa, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by arethusa
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Western Rattlesnake Plantain
records.summary: Goodyera oblongifolia is a species of orchid known by the common names western rattlesnake plantain and giant rattlesnake plantain. It is native to much of North America, particularly in the mountains of the western United States and Canada, from Alaska to northern Mexico, as well as in the Great Lakes region, Maine, Quebec and the Canadian Maritime Provinces.
records.photo_credit: (c) Richard Droker, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-ND)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Field chickweed
records.summary: Cerastium arvense is a species of flowering plant in the pink family known by the common names field mouse-ear and field chickweed. It is a widespread species, occurring throughout Europe and North America, as well as parts of South America.
records.photo_credit: (c) Tig, all rights reserved, uploaded by Tig
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Thimbleberry
records.summary: Rubus parviflorus, commonly called thimbleberry, is a species of Rubus native to North America.
records.photo_credit: (c) Diego Codeco, all rights reserved, uploaded by Diego Codeco
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Firewheel
records.summary: Gaillardia pulchella (firewheel, Indian blanket, Indian blanketflower, or sundance), is a North American species of short-lived perennial or annual flowering plants in the sunflower family. It is native to northern Mexico (Chihuahua, Coahuila, Nuevo León, Sonora, Tamaulipas) and the southern and central United States from Arizona east to Florida and the Carolinas and north as far as Nebraska.
records.photo_credit: (c) TexasEagle, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Woodland pinedrops
records.summary: Pterospora, commonly known as pinedrops, wooodland pinedrops, Albany beechdrops, or giant bird's nest is a North American genus in the subfamily Monotropoidiae of the blueberry family, and includes only the species Pterospora andromedea. It grows in coniferous or mixed forests.
records.photo_credit: (c) Yves Bas, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Yves Bas
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Eastern Cottonwood
records.summary: Populus deltoides, the eastern cottonwood or necklace poplar, is a cottonwood poplar native to North America, growing throughout the eastern, central, and southwestern United States, the southernmost part of eastern Canada, and northeastern Mexico. It is a eudicot.
records.photo_credit: (c) JanetandPhil, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-ND)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Alderleaf Mountain Mahogany
records.summary: Cercocarpus montanus is a North American species of shrub or small tree in the family Rosaceae native to northern Mexico and the western United States. It is known by the common names alder-leaf mountain-mahogany, alder-leaf cercocarpus, and true mountain-mahogany.
records.photo_credit: (c) Carol Jacobs-Carre, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-ND)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Common Lady Fern
records.summary: Athyrium filix-femina, the lady fern or common lady-fern, is a large, feathery species of fern native throughout most of the temperate Northern Hemisphere, where it is often abundant (one of the more common ferns) in damp, shady woodland environments and is often grown for decoration.
records.photo_credit: (c) jacquelinerose, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by jacquelinerose
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Rough horsetail
records.summary: Equisetum hyemale, commonly known as rough horsetail, scouring rush, scouringrush horsetail and in South Africa as snake grass, is a perennial herb in the fern Division Pteridophyta. It is a native plant throughout the Holarctic Kingdom, found in North America, Europe, and northern Asia.
records.photo_credit: (c) Tom Kaye, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Tom Kaye
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Common bracken
records.summary: Pteridium aquilinum (bracken, brake or common bracken), also known as eagle fern, and Eastern brakenfern, is a species of fern occurring in temperate and subtropical regions in both hemispheres. The extreme lightness of its spores has led to its global distribution.
records.photo_credit: (c) c michael hogan, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-SA), uploaded by c michael hogan
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Field horsetail
records.summary: Equisetum arvense, the field horsetail or common horsetail, is an herbaceous perennial horsetail native throughout the arctic and temperate regions of the northern hemisphere. It has separate sterile non-reproductive and fertile spore-bearing stems growing from a perennial underground rhizomatous stem system.
records.photo_credit: (c) rochelle77, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Common selfheal
records.summary: Prunella vulgaris (known as common self-heal, heal-all, woundwort, heart-of-the-earth, carpenter's herb, brownwort and blue curls) is an herbaceous plant in the genus Prunella.
records.photo_credit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Brady Reed
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Common yarrow
records.summary: Achillea millefolium, commonly known as yarrow /ˈjæroʊ/ or common yarrow, is a flowering plant in the family Asteraceae. It is native to temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere in Asia, Europe, and North America.
records.photo_credit: (c) Steve Guttman, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-ND)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Pearly everlasting
records.summary: Anaphalis margaritacea, commonly known as the western pearly everlasting or pearly everlasting, is an Asian and North American species of flowering perennial plant in the sunflower family.
records.photo_credit: (c) esgud, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Pineapple-weed
records.summary: Matricaria discoidea, commonly known as pineappleweed, wild chamomile, and disc mayweed is an annual plant native to North America and Northeast Asia but which has become a cosmopolitan weed. It is in the family Asteraceae.
records.photo_credit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Anne Parsons
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Giant ragweed
records.summary: Ambrosia trifida, the giant ragweed, is a species of flowering plant in the sunflower family. It is native to North America, where it is widespread in Canada, the United States, and northern Mexico.
records.photo_credit: (c) thaven, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Common cowparsnip
records.summary: Heracleum maximum, cow parsnip (also known as Indian celery, Indian rhubarb or pushki) is the only member of the genus Heracleum native to North America. Its classification has caused some difficulty, with recent authoritative sources referring to it variously as Heracleum maximum or Heracleum lanatum, or as either a subspecies, H. sphondylium subsp. montanum, or a variety, H. sphondylium var. lanatum, of the common hogweed (H. sphondylium).
records.photo_credit: (c) rangerkelly, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by rangerkelly
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Rosy Pussytoes
records.summary: Antennaria rosea is a North American species of flowering plant in the daisy family known by the common name rosy pussytoes. It is widespread across much of Canada including all three Arctic territories, as well as Greenland, the western and north-central United States, and the Mexican State of Baja California.
records.photo_credit: (c) Kerry Givens, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Kerry Givens
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Star-flowered lily-of-the-valley
records.summary: Maianthemum stellatum (star-flowered, starry, or little false Solomon's seal, or simply false Solomon's seal; star-flowered lily-of-the-valley or starry false lily of the valley; syn. Smilacina stellata) is a species of flowering plant, native across North America generally from Alaska to California to North Carolina to Newfoundland, plus northern Mexico (Sonora, Chihuahua, Coahuila, Nuevo León).
records.photo_credit: (c) Anita, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: American vetch
records.summary: Vicia americana is a species of legume in the vetch genus known by the common names American vetch and purple vetch. It includes a subspecies known as mat vetch.
records.photo_credit: (c) Andrea Romero, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Andrea Romero
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Hookedspur violet
records.summary: Viola adunca is a species of violet known by the common names hookedspur violet, early blue violet, sand violet, and western dog violet. It is native to meadows and forests of western North America, Canada, and the northern contiguous United States.
records.photo_credit: (c) Ryan Sawby, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Ryan Sawby
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Beaked hazelnut
records.summary: Corylus cornuta, the beaked hazelnut, is a deciduous shrubby hazel found in most of North America, from southern Canada south to Georgia and California. It grows in dry woodlands and forest edges and can reach 4–8 metres (13–26 ft) tall with stems 10–25 centimetres (3.9–9.8 in) thick with smooth gray bark.
records.photo_credit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Lynn Harper
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Red osier dogwood
records.summary: Cornus sericea, the red osier or red-osier dogwood, is a species of flowering plant in the family Cornaceae, native to much of North America. It has sometimes been considered a synonym of the Asian species Cornus alba.
records.photo_credit: (c) adrianakolev, all rights reserved
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: American elm
records.summary: Ulmus americana, generally known as the American elm or, less commonly, as the white elm or water elm, is a species native to eastern North America, naturally occurring from Nova Scotia west to Alberta and Montana, and south to Florida and central Texas. The American elm is an extremely hardy tree that can withstand winter temperatures as low as −42 °C (−44 °F).
records.photo_credit: (c) William Van Hemessen, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by William Van Hemessen
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Common ragweed
records.summary: Ambrosia artemisiifolia, with the common names common ragweed, annual ragweed, and low ragweed, is a species of the genus Ambrosia native to regions of the Americas.
records.photo_credit:
(c) 
Qwert1234, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Prairie false dandelion
records.summary: Nothocalais cuspidata, the prairie false dandelion, is a herbaceous perennial with yellow flowers and long slender leaves, native to the Great Plains.
records.photo_credit: (c) Joshua Mayer, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Red raspberry
records.summary: Rubus idaeus (raspberry, also called red raspberry or occasionally European red raspberry to distinguish it from other raspberry species) is a red-fruited species of Rubus native to Europe and northern Asia and commonly cultivated in other temperate regions.
records.photo_credit: (c) Анна Синичкина, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Анна Синичкина
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Smooth sumac
records.summary: Rhus glabra, the smooth sumac, (also known as white sumac, upland sumac, or scarlet sumac) is a species of sumac in the family Anacardiaceae, native to North America, from southern Quebec west to southern British Columbia in Canada, and south to northern Florida and Arizona in the United States and Tamaulipas in northeastern Mexico.
records.photo_credit: (c) Thomas Shahan, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Thomas Shahan
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: American hophornbeam
records.summary: Ostrya virginiana, the American hophornbeam, is a species of Ostrya native to eastern North America, from Nova Scotia west to southern Manitoba and eastern Wyoming, southeast to northern Florida and southwest to eastern Texas. Populations from Mexico and Central America are also regarded as the same species, although some authors prefer to separate them as a distinct species, Ostrya guatemalensis.
records.photo_credit: (c) Patrick Coin, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-SA)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Bur oak
records.summary: Quercus macrocarpa, the bur oak or burr oak, is a species of oak tree native to central and eastern North America. It is in the white oak section, Quercus sect.
records.photo_credit: (c) rayrob, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by rayrob
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Honey locust
records.summary: The honey locust (Gleditsia triacanthos), also known as the thorny locust, is a deciduous tree in the Fabaceae family, native to central North America where it is mostly found in the moist soil of river valleys. Honey locust is highly adaptable to different environments, has been introduced worldwide, and is an aggressive invasive species.
records.photo_credit: (c) César Andrés Castillo, all rights reserved, uploaded by César Andrés Castillo
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Green ash
records.summary: Fraxinus pennsylvanica, the green ash or red ash, is a species of ash native to eastern and central North America, from Nova Scotia west to southeastern Alberta and eastern Colorado, south to northern Florida, and southwest to Oklahoma and eastern Texas. It has spread and become naturalized in much of the western United States and also in Europe from Spain to Russia.
records.photo_credit: (c) kjsytsma, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by kjsytsma
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Fire cherry
records.summary: Prunus pensylvanica, also known as bird cherry, fire cherry, pin cherry, and red cherry, is a North American cherry species in the genus Prunus.
records.photo_credit: (c) cgbb2004, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by cgbb2004
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Chokecherry
records.summary: Prunus virginiana, commonly called bitter-berry, chokecherry, Virginia bird cherry, and western chokecherry (also black chokecherry for P. virginiana var. demissa), is a species of bird cherry (Prunus subgenus Padus) native to North America. The natural historic range of P. virginiana includes most of Canada (including Northwest Territories, but excluding Yukon, Nunavut, and Labrador), most of the United States (including Alaska, but excluding some states in the Southeast), and northern Mexico (Sonora, Chihuahua, Baja California, Durango, Zacatecas, Coahuila, and...
records.photo_credit: (c) Dan Mullen, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-ND)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Quaking aspen
records.summary: Populus tremuloides is a deciduous tree native to cooler areas of North America, one of several species referred to by the common name aspen. It is commonly called quaking aspen, trembling aspen, American aspen, Quakies, mountain or golden aspen, trembling poplar, white poplar, popple, as well as others.
records.photo_credit: (c) Nathan Perkins, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Nathan Perkins
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Peachleaf willow
records.summary: Salix amygdaloides, the peachleaf willow, is a species of willow native to southern Canada and the United States, from Quebec west to western British Columbia, southeast to eastern Kentucky, and southwest and west to Arizona and Nevada, respectively.
records.photo_credit: (c) Colin Croft, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Colin Croft
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Bebb's willow
records.summary: Salix bebbiana is a species of willow indigenous to Canada and the northern United States, from Alaska and Yukon south to California and Arizona and northeast to Newfoundland and New England. Common names include beaked willow, long-beaked willow, gray willow, and Bebb's willow.
records.photo_credit: (c) Ken Oeser, all rights reserved, uploaded by Ken Oeser
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Common hackberry
records.summary: Celtis occidentalis, commonly known as the common hackberry, is a large deciduous tree native to North America. It is also known as the nettletree, sugarberry, beaverwood, northern hackberry, and American hackberry.
records.photo_credit:
(c) 

Ayotte, Gilles, 1948-, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Golden currant
records.summary: Ribes aureum, known by the common names golden currant, clove currant, pruterberry and buffalo currant, is a species in the genus Ribes. It is native to Canada, most of the United States (except the southeast) and northern Mexico.
records.photo_credit: (c) joeverica, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by joeverica
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Rough cinquefoil
records.summary: Potentilla norvegica is a species of cinquefoil known by the common names rough cinquefoil, ternate-leaved cinquefoil, and Norwegian cinquefoil. It is native to Europe, Asia, and parts of North America, and it can be found elsewhere as an introduced species.
records.photo_credit: (c) Michael John Oldham, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Michael John Oldham
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Monument plant
records.summary: Frasera speciosa is a species of flowering plant in the Gentian Family (Gentianaceae) known by the common names elkweed, deer's ears, and monument plant.
records.photo_credit: (c) Scott F Smith, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Scott F Smith
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Common Liverwort
records.summary: Marchantia polymorpha, sometimes known as the common liverwort or umbrella liverwort, is a large liverwort with a wide distribution around the world. It is variable in appearance and has several subspecies.
records.photo_credit: (c) Ryzhkov Oleg, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Ryzhkov Oleg
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Giant blue sage
records.summary: Salvia azurea, the azure blue sage, azure sage, blue sage or prairie sage, is a herbaceous perennial in the genus Salvia that is native to Central and Eastern North America.
records.photo_credit: (c) Brian Peterson, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-ND)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Prairie Junegrass
records.summary: Koeleria macrantha is a species of grass known by the common name prairie Junegrass in North America and crested hair-grass in the UK. It is widespread across much of Eurasia and North America.
records.photo_credit: (c) rfors55, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: American brooklime
records.summary: Veronica americana, variously called American brooklime or American speedwell, is a plant native to temperate and arctic Asia and North America where it grows in streams and bottomlands.
records.photo_credit: (c) nodaknaturalist, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Prairie smoke
records.summary: Geum triflorum, (prairie smoke, three-flowered avens, or old man's whiskers) is a spring-blooming perennial herbaceous plant of North America from northern Canada to California and east to New York. The flowers bloom from mid-spring to early summer.
records.photo_credit: (c) Nicola Rammell, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Nicola Rammell
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Western blue flag
records.summary: Iris missouriensis (syn. I. montana) is a hardy flowering rhizomatous species of the genus Iris, in the family Iridaceae.
records.photo_credit: (c) stellaginella, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by stellaginella
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Red-berried elder
records.photo_credit: no rights reserved, uploaded by neotrigonia
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Tarragon
records.summary: Tarragon (Artemisia dracunculus), also known as estragon, is a species of perennial herb in the sunflower family. It is widespread in the wild across much of Eurasia and North America, and is cultivated for culinary and medicinal purposes.
records.photo_credit: (c) Danila Popov, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Danila Popov
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Rough cocklebur
records.summary: Xanthium strumarium (rough cocklebur, clotbur, common cocklebur, large cocklebur, woolgarie bur) is a species of annual plants belonging to the Asteraceae family. It probably originates in North America and has been extensively naturalized elsewhere.
records.photo_credit: (c) Oliver Stöhr, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Oliver Stöhr
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Rubber Rabbitbrush
records.summary: Ericameria nauseosa (formerly Chrysothamnus nauseosus), commonly known as Chamisa, rubber rabbitbrush, and gray rabbitbrush, is a North American shrub in the sunflower family (Aster). It grows in the arid regions of western Canada, western United States (from the western Great Plains to the Pacific) and northern Mexico.

records.title: Common Sunflower
records.summary: Helianthus annuus, the common sunflower, is a large annual forb of the genus Helianthus grown as a crop for its edible oil and edible fruits (sunflower seeds). This sunflower species is also used as bird food, as livestock forage (as a meal or a silage plant), and in some industrial applications.

records.title: Squirreltail
records.summary: Elymus elymoides is a species of wild rye known by the common name squirreltail. This grass is native to most of North America west of the Mississippi River and occurs in a number of ecosystems, from the alpine zone to desert sage scrub to valley grassland.

records.title: Common juniper
records.summary: Juniperus communis, the common juniper, is a species of conifer in the genus Juniperus, in the family Cupressaceae. records.title: Western poison ivy
records.summary: Toxicodendron rydbergii the western poison ivy, is a species of Toxicodendron in the cashew family. It is native to most of Canada from the Maritimes to British Columbia, and most of the contiguous United States except the southeastern states, New Jersey, Delaware, and California.

records.title: Fragrant sumac
records.summary: Rhus aromatica, the fragrant sumac, is a deciduous shrub in the family Anacardiaceae native to Canada and the United States from southeast Ontario to Vermont down into central Florida to west Texas up through Nebraska over to southern Wisconsin back to Ontario. It grows in upland open woods, fields, barrens, and rocky cliffs.

records.title: Brittle bladderfern

records.title: Sleepy catchfly

records.title: Cutleaf water parsnip
records.summary: Berula erecta, known as lesser water-parsnip or cutleaf waterparsnip or narrow-leaved water-parsnip, is a member of the carrot family. Growing to around 1 m (3 ft) tall, it is found in or by water.

records.title: Hemp dogbane
records.summary: Apocynum cannabinum (dogbane, amy root, hemp dogbane, prairie dogbane, Indian hemp, rheumatism root, or wild cotton) is a perennial herbaceous plant that grows throughout much of North America - in the southern half of Canada and throughout the United States. records.title: Wild Licorice

It is also sometimes known in the United States as "wild licorice", to distinguish it from the related European liquorice (Glycyrrhiza glabra) which is occasionally cultivated.

records.title: Meadow Deathcamas

records.title: Violet woodsorrel
records.summary: Oxalis violacea, the violet wood-sorrel, is a perennial plant and herb in the Oxalidaceae family. Oxalis species are also known as sour grass, sour trefoil, and shamrock.
records.photo_credit: (c) walkmic, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Ostrich fern
records.summary: Matteuccia is a genus of ferns with one species, Matteuccia struthiopteris (common names ostrich fern, fiddlehead fern or shuttlecock fern). It is a crown-forming, colony-forming plant, occurring in temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere in central and northern Europe, northern Asia, and northern North America.
records.photo_credit: (c) Tom Norton, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Tom Norton
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Sensitive fern
records.summary: Onoclea sensibilis, the sensitive fern, also known as the bead fern, is a coarse-textured, medium to large-sized deciduous perennial fern. The name comes from the observation by early American settlers that it was very sensitive to frost, the fronds dying quickly when first touched by it.
records.photo_credit: (c) Laura Clark, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Laura Clark
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Purple-stem cliffbrake
records.summary: Pellaea atropurpurea, commonly known as purple-stem cliffbrake or just purple cliffbrake, is a fern native to North and Central America. Brake is an old word for fern, related to the word bracken.
records.photo_credit: no rights reserved
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Gunnison's Mariposa Lily
records.summary: Calochortus gunnisonii (Gunnison's mariposa lily) is a North American species of flowering plant in the lily family. It is native to the western United States, primarily in the Rocky Mountains and Black Hills: Arizona, New Mexico, Utah, Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, South Dakota, northwestern Nebraska (Sioux County) and eastern Idaho (Fremont County).
records.photo_credit: (c) irishboy1, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Prairie rose
records.summary: Rosa arkansana, the prairie rose or wild prairie rose, is a species of rose native to a large area of central North America, between the Appalachian and Rocky Mountains from Alberta, Manitoba, and Saskatchewan south to New Mexico, Texas and Indiana. There are two varieties:
records.photo_credit: (c) pipen3107, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Sego Lily
records.summary: Calochortus nuttallii — known as sego lily — is a bulbous perennial which is endemic to the Western United States.
records.photo_credit: (c) Will Pearce, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Will Pearce
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Drummond's Milkvetch
records.summary: Astragalus drummondii is a species of flowering plant in the legume family known by the common name Drummond's milkvetch. The botanist Thomas Drummond first identified the plant during his travels in North America from 1825 to 1835, the year of his death.
records.photo_credit: (c) theziz, all rights reserved
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Aspen fleabane
records.summary: Erigeron speciosus is a widespread North American species of flowering plants in the daisy family known by the common names aspen fleabane, garden fleabane, and showy fleabane.It has been found in western Canada and the United States, from Alberta and British Columbia south as far as Arizona and New Mexico, with some isolated populations in the state of Baja California in Mexico.
records.photo_credit: (c) John Cheeseman, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by John Cheeseman
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Slender yellow woodsorrel
records.summary: Oxalis dillenii, also the southern wood-sorrel and slender yellow woodsorrel, is part of the wood-sorrel family Oxalidaceae, in the genus Oxalis. The appearance of this species is consistent with the clover-like look of the family.
records.photo_credit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Wild bergamot
records.summary: Monarda fistulosa, the wild bergamot or bee balm, is a wildflower in the mint family (Lamiaceae) widespread and abundant as a native plant in much of North America. This plant, with showy summer-blooming pink to lavender flowers, is often used as a honey plant, medicinal plant, and garden ornamental.
records.photo_credit: (c) ziggymom, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Grey-headed coneflower
records.summary: Ratibida pinnata is a species of flowering plant in the aster family known by the common names pinnate prairie coneflower, gray-head coneflower, yellow coneflower, and prairie coneflower. It is native to the central and eastern United States and Ontario in Canada.
records.photo_credit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Andy Wilson
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Nodding onion
records.summary: Allium cernuum, known as nodding onion or lady's leek, is a perennial plant in the genus Allium. It grows in dry woods, rock outcroppings, and prairies.
records.photo_credit: (c) Grace Chovil, all rights reserved, uploaded by Grace Chovil
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Cutleaf coneflower
records.summary: Rudbeckia laciniata, commonly called cutleaf coneflower, is a species of flowering plant in the aster family (Asteraceae). It is native to North America, where it is widespread in both Canada and the United States.
records.photo_credit: (c) kenttrulsson, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by kenttrulsson
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: White spruce
records.summary: Picea glauca, the white spruce, is a species of spruce native to the northern temperate and boreal forests in North America. Picea glauca was originally native from central Alaska all through the east, across southern/central Canada to the Avalon Peninsula in Newfoundland.
records.photo_credit: (c) Shuk Han (Nancy) Mak, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Shuk Han (Nancy) Mak
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Spotted Joe-Pye weed
records.summary: Eutrochium maculatum (spotted joe-pyeweed) is a North American species of flowering plants in the sunflower family. It is widespread through much of the United States and Canada.
records.photo_credit: (c) Adrian Sydor, all rights reserved, uploaded by Adrian Sydor
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Wood horsetail
records.summary: Equisetum sylvaticum, the wood horsetail, is a horsetail (family Equisetaceae) native to the Northern Hemisphere, occurring in North America and Eurasia. Because of its lacy appearance, it is considered among the most attractive of the horsetails.
records.photo_credit: (c) Degtyarev Nikolai Ivanovich, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Degtyarev Nikolai Ivanovich
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Mountain Deathcamas
records.summary: Anticlea elegans, formerly Zigadenus elegans, is also known as mountain deathcamas, elegant camas or "alkali grass". It is not a grass (though its leaves are grass-like), but belongs to the trillium family, Melanthiaceae.
records.photo_credit: (c) Hunter Jarratt, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Hunter Jarratt
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Blue spruce
records.summary: The blue spruce, green spruce, white spruce, Colorado spruce, or Colorado blue spruce, with the scientific name Picea pungens, is a species of spruce tree. It is native to the Rocky Mountains of the United States.
records.photo_credit: (c) Stephen Petersen, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Stephen Petersen
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Aromatic Aster
records.summary: Symphyotrichum oblongifolium, the aromatic aster, is a species of Aster native to parts of eastern and central United States. It is found in parts of Kansas,Ohio, northern Illinois, hilly parts of southern Illinois, and on the banks of the Mississippi River and Illinois River, as well as other parts of the central United States, for example, in Missouri and other places including along the Ohio River, from Pennsylvania to Nebraska to Minnesota to Virginia.
records.photo_credit: (c) Bart Jones, all rights reserved
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Heart-leaf golden Alexanders
records.summary: Zizia is a genus of flowering plants in the parsley family, Apiaceae. It was named after Johann Baptist Ziz (1779–1829), a German botanist from the Rhineland.
records.photo_credit: (c) Daniel McNair, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Daniel McNair
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Glaucous Honeysuckle
records.photo_credit: (c) Tom Fishburn, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Tom Fishburn
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: American groundnut
records.summary: Apios americana, sometimes called the potato bean, hopniss, Indian potato, hodoimo, America-hodoimo, American groundnut,or groundnut (but not to be confused with other plants sometimes known by the name groundnut) is a perennial vine that bears edible beans and large edible tubers. Its vine can grow to 1–6 m long, with pinnate leaves 8–15 cm long with 5–7 leaflets.
records.photo_credit: (c) Ashley Scholer, all rights reserved, uploaded by Ashley Scholer
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Wild sarsaparilla
records.summary: Aralia nudicaulis (commonly wild sarsaparilla, false sarsaparilla, shot bush, small spikenard, wild liquorice, and rabbit root) is a flowering plant of northern and eastern North America which reaches a height of 30–60 cm (12–24 in) with creeping underground stems.
records.photo_credit: (c) birdie111, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Riverbank grape
records.summary: Vitis riparia Michx, with common names riverbank grape or frost grape, is a native American climbing or trailing vine, widely distributed across central and eastern Canada and the central and northeastern parts of the United States, from Quebec to Texas, and eastern Montana to Nova Scotia. There are reports of isolated populations in the northwestern USA, but these are probably naturalized.
records.photo_credit: (c) roomthily, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by roomthily
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Snow-on-the-mountain
records.summary: Euphorbia marginata (commonly known as snow-on-the-mountain, smoke-on-the-prairie, variegated spurge, or whitemargined spurge) is a small annual in the spurge family.
records.photo_credit: (c) Doug Grinbergs, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Doug Grinbergs
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Closed bottle gentian
records.summary: Gentiana andrewsii, the bottle gentian, closed gentian, or closed bottle gentian, is an herbaceous species of flowering plant in the gentian family Gentianaceae. Gentiana andrewsii is native to northeastern North America, from the Dakotas to the East Coast and through eastern Canada.
records.photo_credit: (c) Bonnie Kinder, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Bonnie Kinder
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Western Spiderwort
records.summary: Tradescantia occidentalis, the prairie spiderwort or western spiderwort, is a plant in the dayflower family, Commelinaceae. It is common and widespread across the western Great Plains of the United States, as well as in Arizona, New Mexico, southern Utah, and Sonora, but is listed as a threatened species in Canada.
records.photo_credit: (c) Tabby Brobston, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Tabby Brobston
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Big bluestem
records.summary: Andropogon gerardi, known commonly as big bluestem, turkeyfoot, tall bluestem, and bluejoint, is a tall grass (family Poaceae) native to much of the Great Plains and prairie regions of central North America and grasslands, savannas and woodlands throughout eastern North America.
records.photo_credit: (c) Kingsbrae Garden, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-SA)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Smooth cliffbrake
records.summary: Pellaea glabella is the smooth cliffbrake. For much of pteridological history, it was regarded as a reduced form or variety of Pellaea atropurpurea.
records.photo_credit: (c) Sadie Hickey, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Sadie Hickey
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Stairstep moss
records.summary: Hylocomium splendens, commonly known as glittering woodmoss, splendid feather moss, stairstep moss, and mountain fern moss, is a perennial clonal moss with a widespread distribution in Northern Hemisphere boreal forests. It is commonly found in Europe, Russia, Alaska and Canada, where it is often the most abundant moss species.
records.photo_credit: (c) herdofnoni, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Little bluestem
records.summary: Schizachyrium scoparium, commonly known as little bluestem or beard grass, is a North American prairie grass native to most of the United States, except California, Nevada, and Oregon, and a small area north of the Canada–US border. Its greatest manifestation has always been in the Midwestern prairies.
records.photo_credit: (c) Scott E Severs, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Scott E Severs
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Indiangrass
records.summary: Sorghastrum nutans, known as Indiangrass, is a North American prairie grass found in the United States and Canada, especially in the Great Plains and tallgrass prairies. It is sometimes called Indian grass, yellow Indian-grass, or wood grass.
records.photo_credit: (c) Erica Fraley, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Erica Fraley
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Swamp milkweed
records.summary: Asclepias incarnata, the swamp milkweed, rose milkweed, rose milkflower, swamp silkweed, or white Indian hemp, is a herbaceous perennial plant species native to North America. It grows in damp to wet soils and also is cultivated as a garden plant for its flowers, which attract butterflies and other pollinators with nectar.
records.photo_credit: (c) aarongunnar, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by aarongunnar
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Dakota mock vervain
records.summary: Glandularia bipinnatifida, commonly called Dakota mock vervain, is a species of flowering plant in the verbena family (Verbenaceae).
records.photo_credit: (c) Katelyn Rose, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Katelyn Rose
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Stiff-leaved goldenrod
records.summary: Solidago rigida, also known by the common names stiff goldenrod and stiff-leaved goldenrod is a North American plant species in the Goldenrod family. It is native to the region between the Atlantic Coast and the Rockies, from Alberta east to Ontario, south as far as New Mexico, Texas, and Georgia.
records.photo_credit: (c) eknuth, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by eknuth
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Switchgrass
records.summary: Panicum virgatum, commonly known as switchgrass, is a perennial warm season bunchgrass native to North America, where it occurs naturally from 55°N latitude in Canada southwards into the United States and Mexico. Switchgrass is one of the dominant species of the central North American tallgrass prairie and can be found in remnant prairies, in native grass pastures, and naturalized along roadsides.
records.photo_credit: (c) aarongunnar, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by aarongunnar
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Heath aster
records.summary: Symphyotrichum ericoides (syn. Aster ericoides), known as white heath aster, white aster or heath aster, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae, native to much of North America.
records.photo_credit: (c) August Dorien, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by August Dorien
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Scarlet Globemallow
records.summary: Sphaeralcea coccinea, the scarlet globemallow, is a perennial plant growing 10–30 cm tall from spreading rhizomes with a low habit. They have grayish stems with dense, star-shaped hairs and alternately arranged leaves.
records.photo_credit: (c) Lena Zappia, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Lena Zappia
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Blue clematis
records.summary: Clematis columbiana, the Rocky Mountain clematis, is a species in the buttercup family from the western United States.
records.photo_credit: (c) Steve Ganley, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Steve Ganley
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Field Pussytoes
records.summary: Antennaria neglecta is a North American species of flowering plants in the daisy family known by the common name field pussytoes. It is widespread across much of Canada (including Northwest Territories plus all provinces except Newfoundland/Labrador) as well as the northeastern and north-central United States.
records.photo_credit: (c) Jennifer Danhaus, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Jennifer Danhaus
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Strict blue-eyed grass
records.summary: Sisyrinchium montanum, or American blue-eyed-grass, or strict blue-eyed grass, is a grass-like species of plants from the genus Sisyrinchium native to northern North America from Newfoundland west to easternmost Alaska, and south to Pennsylvania in the east, and to New Mexico in the Rocky Mountains.
records.photo_credit: (c) Léo-Guy de Repentigny, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Léo-Guy de Repentigny
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Nuttall's Violet
records.summary: Viola nuttallii (Nuttall's violet or yellow prairie violet) is a perennial herbaceous plant in the violet family (Violaceae), and is one of the few violet species with lanceolate leaves. It is native to the western Canada and the north-central and western United States.
records.photo_credit: (c) Grant Beverage, all rights reserved, uploaded by Grant Beverage
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Inland ceanothus
records.summary: Ceanothus herbaceus, also known as Jersey tea, is a species of shrub in the buckthorn family, Rhamnaceae and is similar to C. americanus and C. sanguineus. It is a perennial shrub which is native to North America....
records.photo_credit: (c) lisajasiurkowski, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Mintweed
records.summary: Salvia reflexa, the lanceleaf sage, Rocky Mountain sage, blue sage, lambsleaf sage, sage mint or mintweed, is a perennial subshrub native to the United States and Mexico and introduced to Argentina, Australia, Canada, South Africa and New Zealand.
records.photo_credit: (c) Lee Hoy, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC-ND), uploaded by Lee Hoy
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Clammy groundcherry
records.summary: Physalis heterophylla, colloquial name clammy groundcherry, is a herbaceous plant that is a member of the Solanaceae family. It is native to North America, occurring primarily in the eastern United States and Canada.
records.photo_credit: (c) Susan Elliott, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Susan Elliott
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Canada wild rye
records.summary: Elymus canadensis is a species of wild rye known by the common name Canada wild rye. This grass is native to much of North America, being most abundant in the central plains and Great Plains.
records.photo_credit: (c) Annette Le Faive, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Annette Le Faive
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Smooth blue aster
records.summary: Symphyotrichum laeve (smooth blue aster, smooth aster, smooth-leaved aster, glaucous Michaelmas-daisy or glaucous aster) is a flowering plant native to Canada and the United States.
records.photo_credit: (c) Eric Lamb, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Eric Lamb
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Maximilian sunflower
records.summary: Helianthus maximiliani is a North American species of sunflower known by the common name Maximilian sunflower.

records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Maryland Sanicle
records.summary: Sanicula marilandica, the Maryland sanicle or Maryland black snakeroot, is a flowering plant widespread in North America but rare along the Pacific coast of the continent and Texas. Sanicula marilandica is listed as Sensitive in Washington state.
records.photo_credit: (c) Varina Crisfield, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Varina Crisfield
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Field goldenrod
records.summary: Solidago nemoralis is a species of flowering plant in the aster family, Asteraceae. It is native to North America, where it is widely found in Canada (every province except Newfoundland and Labrador) and the United States (all states wholly or partially east of the Rocky Mountains).
records.photo_credit: (c) Mark Kluge, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Mark Kluge
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Missouri goldenrod
records.summary: Solidago missouriensis is a species of flowering plant in the aster family known by the common names Missouri goldenrod and prairie goldenrod. It is native to North America, where it is widespread across much of Canada, the United States, and northern Mexico.
records.photo_credit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Owen McElroy
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Dotted gayfeather
records.summary: Liatris punctata is a species of flowering plant in the aster family known by the common names dotted gayfeather, dotted blazingstar, and narrow-leaved blazingstar. It is native to North America, where it occurs throughout the plains of central Canada, the central United States, and northern Mexico.
records.photo_credit: (c) palr76, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Rocky Mountain blazing star
records.summary: Liatris ligulistylis, common name Rocky Mountain blazing star, is a flowering plant of the Asteraceae family. Leaves are basal and mostly alternate, linear and sessile nearer the top of the plant, while oblanceolate with petioles nearer the bottom, all with whitish midribs.
records.photo_credit: (c) Corey Lange, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Corey Lange
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Stiff Sunflower
records.summary: Helianthus pauciflorus, called the stiff sunflower is a North American plant species in the sunflower family. It is widespread across the Great Plains, the Rocky Mountains, and the Great Lakes regions, and naturalized in scattered locations in the eastern United States and in much of southern Canada (from Alberta to Nova Scotia).
records.photo_credit: (c) Jeff Steele, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Jeff Steele
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Cylindrical Thimbleweed
records.summary: Anemone cylindrica is an upright growing, clump forming herbaceous plant species in the genus Anemone and family Ranunculaceae. Plants grow 30–100 centimetres (12–39 in) tall, flowering early summer but often found flowering till late summer, the flowers are greenish-white.
records.photo_credit: (c) LeAnn Plinske, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by LeAnn Plinske
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Alpine Milkvetch
records.summary: Astragalus alpinus is a species of flowering plant in the legume family known by the common name alpine milkvetch. It has a circumpolar distribution, occurring throughout the upper latitudes of the Northern Hemisphere.
records.photo_credit: (c) Torsti Salonen, all rights reserved, uploaded by Torsti Salonen

records.title: Spring Coralroot
records.summary: Spring coralroot (Corallorhiza wisteriana) — also called Arousing coralroot or Wister's Coralroot — is a species of coralroot orchid. It is widespread through much of Mexico as well as parts of the United States (Rocky Mountains, Appalachians, the Southeast, and the Mississippi and Ohio Valleys).
records.photo_credit: (c) Ken-ichi Ueda, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Ken-ichi Ueda
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: White-flower Beardtongue
records.summary: Penstemon albidus, commonly known as white penstemon, white-flower beardtongue, or Red-Line Beardtongue is a very widespread perennial flower of the mixed-grass and shortgrass prairies. Its natural distribution is from Manitoba and Alberta in Canada to Texas and New Mexico in the United States.
records.photo_credit: (c) Jack Wilkinson, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Jack Wilkinson
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Creeping mahonia
records.summary: Mahonia repens commonly known as creeping mahonia, creeping Oregon grape, creeping barberry, or prostrate barberry, is a species of Mahonia native to the Rocky Mountains and westward areas of North America, from British Columbia and Alberta in the north through Arizona and New Mexico, then into northwest Mexico by some reports. It is also found in many areas of California and the Great Basin region in Nevada.
records.photo_credit: (c) Matt Lavin, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Rock spikemoss
records.summary: Selaginella rupestris, the northern selaginellla sometimes locally known as ledge spike-moss or rock spike-moss, is a species of spike-moss occurring in dry rocky places in eastern North America, including one locality in Greenland. It has a wide but sporadic range.
records.photo_credit: (c) Lincoln Durey, all rights reserved, uploaded by Lincoln Durey
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Alpine golden buckwheat
records.summary: Eriogonum flavum is a species of wild buckwheat.
records.photo_credit: (c) Stephen B. Brown, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Stephen B. Brown
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Rocky Mountain Juniper
records.summary: Juniperus scopulorum (Rocky Mountain juniper) is a species of juniper native to western North America, in Canada in British Columbia and southwest Alberta, in the United States from Washington east to North Dakota, south to Arizona and also locally western Texas, and northernmost Mexico from Sonora east to Coahuila. It grows at altitudes of 500–2,700 metres (1,600–8,900 ft) on dry soils, often together with other juniper species. "Scopulorum" means "of the mountains.
records.photo_credit: (c) Gabe, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Gabe
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Dense spikemoss
records.summary: Selaginella densa is a species of spikemoss known by the common names lesser spikemoss, prairie spikemoss, and Rocky Mountains spikemoss. It is native to western North America, where it can be found from Alaska to Ontario, the Dakotas, Texas and far northern California.
records.photo_credit: (c) Kieran Schnitzspahn, all rights reserved, uploaded by Kieran Schnitzspahn
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Lambert's Locoweed
records.summary: Oxytropis lambertii is a species of flowering plant in the legume family known by several common names, including purple locoweed, woolly locoweed, and Lambert crazyweed.
records.photo_credit: (c) Will H., all rights reserved, uploaded by Will H.
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Ground-plum
records.summary: Astragalus crassicarpus, known as ground plum or buffalo plum, is a perennial species of flowering plant in the legume family, Fabaceae, native to North America. It was described in 1813.
records.photo_credit: (c) Jon Fearns, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC), uploaded by Jon Fearns
records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.source_label: Native plants of the Black Hills

records.title: Slender stinging nettle
records.summary: Urtica dioica subsp. gracilis, the California nettle or American stinging nettle, is a herbaceous perennial plant native to most of the United States and Canada. records.title: Edible valerian
records.summary: Valeriana edulis, the tobacco root or edible valerian, a species in the Caprifoliaceae family, is a dioecious perennial flowering plant native to western and central North America.
